orders.detail: Infectious Disease Urgent E-Consult: Tick-Borne Co-Infection in Pregnancy

GUI.note:
Assessment
34-year-old G1P0 pregnant female (~20 weeks gestation; 16w6d by dating ultrasound on 2024-05-10 per Obstetrics prenatal intake note) presenting with 7 days of fever (38.6 C), drenching sweats, fatigue, and myalgia two weeks after removing an attached tick while hiking on Nantucket.

1. Early Localized Lyme Disease (Borrelia burgdorferi) - Mild/Uncomplicated:
   - Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic expanding 12 cm erythematous annular patch (erythema migrans) on the right thigh at the tick bite site after endemic Nantucket exposure. No carditis, neurologic, or arthritic manifestations.

2. Babesiosis (Babesia microti) Co-infection - Mild-to-Moderate Severity:
   - Confirmed on peripheral blood smear showing intraerythrocytic ring forms and pathognomonic tetrads (Maltese cross) with 1.6% parasitemia (<4% threshold for severe disease).
   - Associated laboratory findings of mild hemolytic anemia (Hgb 10.1 g/dL, LDH 412 U/L), thrombocytopenia (platelets 96 x10^3/uL), and mild transaminitis (AST 64 U/L, ALT 58 U/L), with normal renal function (Cr 0.6 mg/dL) and stable vital signs without end-organ dysfunction.
   - No neutrophil morulae seen on smear to suggest Anapla
